findings.claim: The new `jsonContentTypeRegex` only accepts the `application/...` tree, so common JSON content types such as `text/json` (and `text/x-json`) that the middleware may previously have pretty-printed (or that callers expect to be pretty-printed) will now be skipped silently.
findings.rationale: Regex is anchored with `^application\/`. If the prior implementation used something like `startsWith('application/json')` this is not a regression, but if it checked `includes('json')` or `text/json` it is. Medium confidence that this is an intentional narrowing, but worth confirming against the tests.

findings.claim: The structured-suffix prefix class `[a-z0-9._-]+` is narrower than the RFC 6838 subtype token set and does not allow `+`, so valid types like `application/vnd.foo+bar+json` or subtypes containing `!`/`#`/`$`/`^` etc. will not be recognized as JSON.
findings.rationale: RFC 6838 restricted-name characters include `!#$&^_+.-` and digits/letters; nested structured suffixes exist in the wild. Low-to-medium confidence this matters in practice, but it is a real coverage gap of the matcher.

findings.claim: The regex requires the media type to start at index 0 with no tolerance for leading whitespace, and the lookahead `(?=$|[;\s])` does not accept `,`. A header value such as ` application/json` (leading space, which some proxies/frameworks produce) or a comma-separated value list will not match.
findings.rationale: Header values are usually trimmed by the runtime's Headers implementation, so this is likely harmless, but if the value is read from a raw object/init it can retain whitespace. Low confidence, but cheap to guard with a `\s*` prefix or a `.trim()` before testing.

findings.claim: The constant is declared at module scope but is not exported and no usage appears in this hunk; if the accompanying call site was not updated, this is dead code and will trip `noUnusedLocals`/lint.
findings.rationale: Cannot see the rest of the file in this hunk, so confidence is low — flagged only so the reviewer verifies the regex is actually wired into the content-type check that replaced the previous string comparison.
